tracks.narration: When y is tangled up with x — no clean formula y of x — can we still get the slope? Yes.
Take an example. F of x and y equals x squared plus x y plus y squared. Set it equal to three. The solution set is a closed curve — a tilted ellipse.

Differentiate both sides with respect to x, treating y as a function of x. The partial in x plus the partial in y times dy by dx equals zero. Solve: dy by dx equals minus the partial in x over the partial in y.

Now slide the point all the way around the curve. The tangent rotates with it. Where the partial in y vanishes the tangent is vertical — undefined slope. Where the partial in x vanishes the tangent is flat. The formula handles every position.
The level curve hides the function y of x. Implicit differentiation reads the slope without ever isolating it.
